text:
Rina Patel: opened PR #842 to add a short 'pricing tier -> alerts' walkthrough. goal is to help customers map the pricing table to dashboard panels and recommended alert thresholds. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/842
Owen Brooks: good idea. can you enumerate the metric names and the recommended alert expressions? product asked for sensible defaults per tier.
Rina Patel: sure. metrics: `rw_quota_consumed_total` (tokens consumed), `rw_request_rate` (requests/sec), and `rw_usage_units_total` (units for enterprise plans). suggested alerts:
- for free tier: alert when `increase(rate(rw_quota_consumed_total[1h])) > 0.15 * monthly_allowance`
- for pro tier: alert when `rate(rw_request_rate[5m]) > 0.7 * reserved_capacity`
- for enterprise: alert when `increase(rw_usage_units_total[1h]) > expected_hourly_burn * 1.25`
Meera Joshi: can you also add a sample Grafana panel JSON we can include in `/assets/grafana/panels/alerting_examples.json`? ops likes copy-paste assets.
Rina Patel: yep added panel JSON and a small README showing how to replace `$workspace` and `$tier` variables. PR includes a screenshot too.
Carlos Vega: tiny nit: in the pricing page footnote you reference headers `X-RW-Quota-*` but the alerts guide refers to `rw_quota_consumed_total`  add a mapping sentence so customers know which header maps to which metric.
Rina Patel: added mapping table: header -> metric -> example dashboard panel. also included quick conversion note: "If you need tokens -> units, see conversion table in appendix."
Owen Brooks: for SDK snippets, can we show how to read the quota header and raise an automatic paging/telemetry event? just a short Python example would be enough.
Meera Joshi: draft Python: ```python
resp = client.generate(prompt)
remaining = int(resp.headers.get('X-RW-Quota-Remaining', '0'))
limit = int(resp.headers.get('X-RW-Quota-Limit', '0'))
if remaining < limit * 0.1:
    telemetry.capture('quota_low', {'remaining': remaining, 'limit': limit})
```
Carlos Vega: looks good. add a fallback for old header names: `resp.headers.get('X-RW-Quota-Remaining') or resp.headers.get('X-Quota-Remaining')`. also mention headers are case-insensitive.
Rina Patel: added fallback and a short troubleshooting checklist: 1) header stripped by CDN/gateway, 2) exporter label mismatch (check metric name), 3) rate alerts firing due to bursty traffic (recommend smoothing window).

Owen Brooks: approved after minor wording tweak on the pro-tier expression.
Meera Joshi: approved. left one suggestion to include an example PagerDuty routing key in the alert README (placeholder only).
Carlos Vega: approved.

Rina Patel: merged. I'll post a short summary in #docs and add a migration item to the internal tracker so infra can ensure metric names are exported with the new canonical names. thanks all :sparkles:
